{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABh95wuQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhLVuFM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 170, "title": "Remember local ROMs in IndexedDB and expose them in the cartridge picker", "body": "## Motivation

Currently, a user can select a personal SNES ROM with **Insert cartridge → Open local ROM…**, and it starts playing immediately. The browser persists battery-backed SRAM, but not the ROM itself. After reloading or revisiting the site, the user has to find and select the same ROM file again.

Allow users to keep their own reusable collection of cartridges in the browser. A successfully loaded local ROM should automatically appear in the existing cartridge picker and be selectable on subsequent visits, without selecting its file again.

Baseline: `main` at `9e1e9dde28098cf3ca28ee4598b58443e8d1c8a0`. The shared loading, SHA-256 identity, ROM validation and SRAM restoration pipeline is in [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), with the picker in [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html).

## Expected UX

- Keep the existing **Insert cartridge** entry point. Do not introduce a separate library page, account, settings screen or extra import confirmation.
- The picker contains the existing bundled demos, a compact list of saved personal cartridges (e.g. **My cartridges**, when nonempty), and **Open local ROM…**.
- Opening a new supported local `.sfc` / `.smc` file validates and starts the game through the normal cartridge-loading path. Once successful, automatically remember the ROM locally; no additional Save button or user gesture is required.
- On subsequent visits or after a reload, the remembered cartridges appear in the same picker. Selecting one loads its stored bytes, restores its SRAM and starts play just like selecting a bundled demo.
- Use the selected file's name as the default display name. Clearly distinguish saved personal cartridges from the bundled demos. Keep long names readable without breaking the layout. No cover art, editing UI, tags, or folders in this iteration.
- Provide an unobtrusive, accessible per-cartridge Remove action. Removing a stored ROM removes it from the list, not the user's original disk file or its SRAM. Prevent an accidental launch when pressing Remove. Use a short confirmation if necessary to avoid accidental deletion. Removing the currently inserted ROM should not stop, reset, or eject the running machine; the user may continue playing.
- Selecting an already inserted identical cartridge should not unexpectedly reset or interrupt it, consistent with the existing picker behavior.
- Retain the current visible inserted-cartridge indicator, predictable auto-play, Play/Pause semantics and normal cancel behavior.

## Storage and identity

Use **IndexedDB** for the ROM bytes and minimal metadata (normalized ROM SHA-256, filename/display name and binary data). Store binary bytes directly rather than base64 ROM strings in localStorage. Keep existing SRAM storage and identity unchanged.

- Use the existing normalized-ROM SHA-256 identity after removing a supported copier header. Deduplicate identical content even if the filename differs or it was imported with/without a copier header. Different ROM content, including a newly built version of a user's homebrew ROM, is a different cartridge; do not silently overwrite an older version or inherit its save by filename. Avoid redundant personal copies of identical bundled ROMs; preserve the existing shared SRAM identity.
- Only persist ROMs successfully accepted by the normal core validation/loading path. Invalid, unsupported or oversized files must not pollute the library or change the current SRAM protection behavior. Preserve existing ROM size and hardware restrictions.
- Load stored cartridges through the same validation, identity and SRAM restoration path as file imports and bundled demos. Verify stored bytes match their expected identity. Do not duplicate the emulator lifecycle or create an alternate unchecked ROM-loading route.
- Keep startup and picker metadata loading lightweight; do not read all ROM binaries into Wasm or memory at startup. Read the selected cartridge on demand.
- Use completed IndexedDB transactions as the source of truth for list changes. Handle pending operations safely so that stale completions, concurrent imports/removals, or reloads cannot create duplicate entries or misrepresent successful writes.
- Never upload a personal ROM, its metadata, or SRAM to a server. Do not require new network services or change the published bundled-ROM assets. Data belongs to this browser profile and origin; it is not cloud-synced.
- Browser storage is best-effort: quota exhaustion, disabled/unavailable IndexedDB, private browsing limitations, eviction and clearing site data may prevent retention. ROM-library persistence failures must not block an otherwise valid game from playing or prevent using the original local-file chooser. Give concise, actionable feedback if the ROM could not be remembered; do not show a successful saved entry until the write commits. If a stored ROM is missing/corrupt, allow recovery by reopening the original file and safely removing the broken entry.
- Preserve existing **SRAM failure protections**. A ROM-library write failure is distinct from an SRAM save/restore failure; do not weaken existing SRAM safety gates. Deleting a ROM must not delete or modify its SRAM. Reimporting the same ROM later restores its existing SRAM, if available.
- Do not change existing SRAM key format, migrate existing saves unnecessarily, or add compatibility layers for hypothetical future storage mechanisms.

## Implementation guidelines

Follow the README's UI/UX principles: **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable.** Use a small, well-defined IndexedDB module or helper and reuse the existing shared cartridge-loading path. Keep the picker accessible by keyboard and touch, scrollable for a growing collection, and within the viewport and safe-area insets. Do not disturb the game screen, twelve-button controls, Scale/Display, volume, fullscreen, or cartridge picker cancellation. Keep ROM storage independent of display and audio settings. No frameworks, remote dependencies, cloud backup, save states, or SRAM import/export as part of this task.

## Acceptance criteria (pre-merge)

- [ ] With a real supported local ROM, importing starts play as before and creates a single durable personal-cartridge entry. Reloading the page and reopening the same origin/browser context shows the entry; selecting it launches the actual stored ROM without a file chooser.
- [ ] Verify several distinct ROMs, identical bytes with different filenames and supported copier-header variants, same-name ROMs with different content, and the bundled-demo identity case. Each cartridge's displayed name, normalized hash and SRAM remain consistent.
- [ ] Save progress in a battery-backed guest, switch to a saved cartridge, reload/revisit, and verify restoration in the real Wasm guest. Remove and reimport the ROM and verify its SRAM is retained. Removing an active ROM does not alter the running guest.
- [ ] Reject invalid/unsupported/oversized files without saving library entries. Exercise missing/corrupt stored data, transaction errors, quota exhaustion, denied/unavailable IndexedDB, cancellation, and repeated selections. The normal local-file and bundled-demo paths remain usable, with truthful feedback; existing SRAM protections remain intact.
- [ ] Verify the browser does not send personal ROM bytes or SRAM in network requests; keep the static GitHub Pages deployment and asset allowlist intact.
- [ ] Validate picker scrolling, long filenames, keyboard focus/navigation, removal affordances, and desktop, narrow portrait and short landscape layouts. No extra permanent settings UI or redundant instructions.
- [ ] Add focused browser integration tests using the real Wasm core and IndexedDB (including reload persistence and storage-failure paths); preserve all existing cartridge, SRAM, playback, display, fullscreen, input and Pages-subpath coverage. Run the required production build and applicable browser/core CI gates. Record actual results and limitations without weakening unrelated tests.
- [ ] Update README with a short explanation that successfully imported ROMs are remembered in this browser, how to select/remove them, and that clearing browser site data may erase stored ROMs and SRAM. Original files should be kept separately.

## Post-merge verification

After merging, verify the new GitHub Pages deployment and exercise the published app: import a legal test ROM, reload, select it from the saved list, remove it, and reimport while retaining its SRAM where applicable. Record the deployed revision, workflow and actual browser results. Track a confirmed regression in a separate linked task rather than reopening completed work solely for pending post-merge checks.

## Related

- #122 — unified cartridge picker and SRAM lifecycle
- #128 — insertion/reset behavior
- #160 — user-controlled playback
- #162 / #164 — minimal player UI and display controls
